module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg tx,
    output reg ready
);
    reg [3:0] bit_index; // To track the current bit position
    reg [10:0] shift_reg; // 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits
    reg sending; // Flag to indicate if we are currently sending data

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            tx <= 1; // Idle state (high)
            ready <= 1; // Ready to send new data
            sending <= 0;
            bit_index <= 0;
        end else if (start && ready) begin
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Load the shift register with stop bit and data
            tx <= 0; // Start bit
            sending <= 1; // Set sending flag
            bit_index <= 0; // Start from the first bit
            ready <= 0; // Not ready until done
        end else if (sending) begin
            if (bit_index < 10) begin
                tx <= shift_reg[bit_index]; // Shift out the next bit
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1; // Move to the next bit
            end else begin
                sending <= 0; // Finished sending
                tx <= 1; // Set tx back to idle state
                ready <= 1; // Ready to send new data
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

- Input: clk (clock), rst (reset), mosi (master out slave in), miso (master in slave out), start (to initiate communication), data_in (data to be sent).

code:
module spi_master (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input mosi,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sclk,
    output reg ss,
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    
    reg [3:0] bit_cnt;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: sending
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            sclk <= 0;
            ss <= 1;
            bit_cnt <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle State
                    ss <= 1;
                    if (start) begin
                        ss <= 0; // Enable slave
                        shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data
                        bit_cnt <= 0;
                        state <= 1; // Move to sending state
                    end

                1: begin // Sending State
                    sclk <= ~sclk; // Generate clock
                    if (sclk) begin // On rising edge

                        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1;
                        if (bit_cnt == 7) begin
                            state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                        end
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
    
endmodule

        end
    end

code:
module KalmanFilter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] noisy_measurement,
    output reg [15:0] filtered_value
);
    parameter Q = 16'h0001; // process noise covariance
    parameter R = 16'h0004; // measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] x; // estimated state
    reg [15:0] p; // estimation error covariance
    reg [15:0] k; // Kalman gain

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            x <= 16'h0000;
            p <= 16'h0001; // initial estimation error covariance
            filtered_value <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            // Prediction update
            p <= p + Q; 

            // Measurement update
            k <= p / (p + R); // Compute Kalman gain
            x <= x + k * (noisy_measurement - x); // Update state estimate
            p <= (16'h0001 - k) * p; // Update estimation error covariance

            filtered_value <= x; // Output the estimated state
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire cs, // chip select
    input wire [7:0] data_in, // data to send

);
    reg [2:0] bit_index; // index to keep track of the bit being sent
    reg [7:0] shift_reg; // shift register for data

    always @(posedge clk or negedge cs) begin
        if (!cs) begin
            // Reset on chip select deactivation
            bit_index <= 3'b000;
            shift_reg <= data_in;
            done <= 1'b0;

                bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
            end else begin
                done <= 1'b1; // Signal completion after sending 8 bits
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [3:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [3:0] M; // Divisor
    reg [3:0] count; // Count for iterations
    reg state; // State to indicate processing

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            A <= 4'b0000;
            Q <= 4'b0000;
            M <= divisor;
            quotient <= 4'b0000;
            remainder <= 4'b0000;
            done <= 0;
            count <= 4; // Number of bits for division
            state <= 1; // Start state
        end else if (state) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                A <= {A[2:0], Q[3]}; // Shift left
                Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left in Q
                A <= A - M; // Subtract divisor from A

                if (A[3] == 1) begin // A < 0
                    A <= A + M; // Restore A
                    Q[0] <= 0; // No change in Q
                end else begin
                    Q[0] <= 1; // Set Q bit
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                quotient <= Q;
                remainder <= A;
                done <= 1; // Indicate division is done
                state <= 0; // End state
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire data_in,
    input wire ack,
    input wire nack,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg err,
    output reg ack_out
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, SEND = 2'b01, WAIT_ACK = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            data_out <= 0;
            err <= 0;
            ack_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Load data to send
                    ack_out <= 0; // Reset ACK output
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    ack_out <= 1; // Send data and wait for ACK
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        ack_out <= 0; // Clear ACK output
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE to send next data
                    end else if (nack) begin
                        err <= 1; // Set error flag on NACK
                        state <= SEND; // Retransmit data
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule

            2'b01: qam_out[7:4] = 4'b0100; // I = 1

Design a simple memory allocation and deallocation system using a FIFO queue structure. The system should support two operations: `malloc` to allocate a memory block and `free` to deallocate a memory block. Each memory block will be represented by a unique identifier (ID). The memory pool can store a fixed number of memory blocks. If `malloc` is called when the pool is full, it should signal an allocation failure. If `free` is called with an identifier that is not currently allocated, it should signal an error.
code:
module memory_management (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input malloc_req,
    input free_req,
    input [3:0] mem_id, // Unique identifier for memory block (0-15)
    output reg [3:0] allocated_id, // ID of allocated block
    output reg alloc_success, // Allocation success flag
    output reg free_success // Free success flag
);
    parameter MAX_MEM_BLOCKS = 4;
    reg [3:0] mem_pool [0:MAX_MEM_BLOCKS-1]; // Memory pool
    reg [1:0] head; // Pointer for FIFO queue
    reg [1:0] tail; // Pointer for FIFO queue
    reg [MAX_MEM_BLOCKS-1:0] allocated; // Allocation status

    // Initialize memory and flags
    integer i;
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            head <= 0;
            tail <= 0;
            alloc_success <= 0;
            free_success <= 0;
            allocated_id <= 0;
            for (i = 0; i < MAX_MEM_BLOCKS; i = i + 1) begin
                allocated[i] <= 0; // All blocks free
            end
        end else begin
            // Handle malloc request
            if (malloc_req) begin
                if (tail - head < MAX_MEM_BLOCKS) begin
                    mem_pool[tail % MAX_MEM_BLOCKS] <= mem_id;
                    allocated[mem_id] <= 1; // Mark as allocated
                    allocated_id <= mem_id;
                    alloc_success <= 1;
                    tail <= tail + 1;
                end else begin
                    alloc_success <= 0; // Allocation failed
                end
            end else begin
                alloc_success <= 0; // Reset allocation success
            end

            // Handle free request
            if (free_req) begin
                if (allocated[mem_id]) begin
                    allocated[mem_id] <= 0; // Mark as free
                    free_success <= 1;
                    head <= head + 1; // Move head for FIFO
                end else begin
                    free_success <= 0; // Free failed, not allocated
                end
            end else begin
                free_success <= 0; // Reset free success
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

- Four channels (channel_0 to channel_3) that can independently request data transfers.
- A clock input to synchronize operations.
- A reset input to initialize the controller.
- Each channel should have a request input (`req`), an acknowledge output (`ack`), and a data output (`data_out`).
- When a channel requests a transfer, it should be granted access in a round-robin manner.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] req,          // Request inputs from each channel
    output reg [3:0] ack,     // Acknowledge outputs
    output reg [7:0] data_out  // Data output for the selected channel
);
    reg [1:0] current_channel; // For round-robin selection
    reg [7:0] memory [0:3];    // Simulated memory for each channel

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            ack <= 4'b0000;
            current_channel <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            ack <= 4'b0000; // Clear all acknowledges
            if (req[current_channel]) begin
                ack[current_channel] <= 1'b1; // Acknowledge the current channel
                data_out <= memory[current_channel]; // Output data
            end
            
            // Move to the next channel in round-robin fashion
            current_channel <= (current_channel + 1) % 4;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a hash table that supports the following operations: inserting a key-value pair, deleting a key, and retrieving a value by key. The hash table should handle collisions using separate chaining with linked lists. The table should have a fixed size, and the input key will be 8 bits wide, while the value will be 32 bits wide. The operations will be controlled by a 2-bit opcode: 00 for insert, 01 for delete, and 10 for retrieve. The output should provide the status of the operation (success or failure) and the retrieved value if applicable.
code:
module hash_table (
    input wire [7:0] key,
    input wire [31:0] value,
    input wire [1:0] opcode,
    output reg [31:0] out_value,
    output reg success
);

    parameter TABLE_SIZE = 256; // Hash table size
    reg [7:0] keys[TABLE_SIZE];    // Keys Storage
    reg [31:0] values[TABLE_SIZE];  // Values Storage
    reg [31:0] chain[TABLE_SIZE];   // Linked list handling (for simplicity, using direct address)
    integer i;

    initial begin
        for (i = 0; i < TABLE_SIZE; i = i + 1) begin
            keys[i] = 8'b0;
            values[i] = 32'b0;
            chain[i] = 32'b0;
        end
    end

    always @* begin
        success = 1'b0;
        out_value = 32'b0;
        case (opcode)
            2'b00: begin // Insert
                if (keys[key] == 8'b0) begin
                    keys[key] = key;
                    values[key] = value;
                    success = 1'b1; // Success
                end else begin
                    success = 1'b0; // Key already exists
                end
            end
            2'b01: begin // Delete
                if (keys[key] != 8'b0) begin
                    keys[key] = 8'b0;
                    values[key] = 32'b0;
                    success = 1'b1; // Success
                end else begin
                    success = 1'b0; // Key not found
                end
            end
            2'b10: begin // Retrieve
                if (keys[key] != 8'b0) begin
                    out_value = values[key];
                    success = 1'b1; // Success
                end else begin
                    success = 1'b0; // Key not found
                end
            end
            default: begin
                success = 1'b0; // Invalid opcode
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule
